data.title: BOE likely to raise rates further in 2027, Pill tells FT
data.description:
The Bank of England will probably need to raise interest rates further in 2027, over and above an increase at the next meeting in December, to combat inflation, Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill told the Financial Times in an interview published on Saturday.

Britain's central bank raised interest rates to 4% from 3.75% in its November meeting, the first rise since August 2023. Pill told the FT that hike was a “significant step” towards getting monetary policy into a better place, but that “we have further to go.”

“My view would be we will see evidence that motivates further rises” Pill told the newspaper, referring to the need for rate hikes next year, given the risks of second-round effects from elevated energy costs. “We will do what is necessary to get inflation back to 2% through time.”

British inflation, driven by second-round effects on wages caused by the ​Iran war, is likely to ‌rise to around 5% in the middle of next year, according to the BoE, which is more than double the central bank's target.

Pill considered an end to the US-Israeli conflict with Iran and a fall in energy prices to be a “very low probability,” signalling that he is set to vote for another quarter-point increase next month, the FT said.

"My bias, for what it’s worth, is that I worry about the inflationary impact being magnified by second-round effects,” he told the newspaper, adding that he believed that the central bank should have acted sooner to combat inflation. “In my view, we waited too long.”

Markets currently price in 90 basis points of tightening by end 2027, implying rates could get close to 5% in 2027. Pill said these expectations were “not outrageous.”

Because of the delays in hiking borrowing costs, “the ability to be modest [in the scale of rate rises] has diminished," he told the FT.

Pill signalled that he would not seek a third term as the bank’s chief economist when his current term ends in September 2027, according to the report.

data.title: Fed Vice Chair Says AI’s Trillion-Dollar Infrastructure Push Is Adding To Inflation Pressures
data.description:
Key points:
  • Jefferson said expectations of long-term productivity gains from AI are already having a significant impact on economic activity.
  • He pointed to rising equity prices, partly fueled by enthusiasm around the technology, as one factor boosting household wealth and spending.
  • Jefferson highlighted that meanwhile, companies are pouring money into data centers and related infrastructure to support AI model training and inference, driving a sharp increase in business investment.

Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson has warned that the massive artificial intelligence infrastructure buildout is adding to inflationary pressures in the U.S. economy, even as the technology promises to deliver substantial productivity gains over time.

Speaking at the University of California, San Diego, on Friday, Jefferson said the surge in AI-related investment is boosting demand, driving up prices of certain goods and adding to broader price pressures.

However, he expects those inflationary effects to ease as supply catches up and productivity gains begin to materialize.

Jefferson Says AI Boom Is Driving Investment, Household Spending

Jefferson said expectations of long-term productivity gains from AI are already having a significant impact on economic activity.

He pointed to rising equity prices, partly fueled by enthusiasm around the technology, as one factor boosting household wealth and spending.

Jefferson highlighted that meanwhile, companies are pouring money into data centers and related infrastructure to support AI model training and inference, driving a sharp increase in business investment.

“Firms are building and equipping new data centers on a very large scale to support model training and inference, driving rapid growth in aggregate business investment,” Jefferson said.

He added that this spending is already “putting upward pressure on resource utilization and the general price level.”

Memory And Logic Chips Face Supply Constraints

The Fed Vice Chair believes that the inflationary impact is particularly visible in industries struggling to keep pace with surging AI-related demand.

Jefferson pointed to memory and logic chips as examples of sectors where investment demand has outstripped available supply, contributing to steep price increases.

The implications extend beyond the semiconductor industry. Higher costs for components used in technology products and services are feeding into prices across the broader consumer economy.

Jefferson noted that the boom in demand for new technologies has been driving “unusually strong cost increases for consumer goods and services that depend on the same inputs, like memory.”

The pressure comes at a time when inflation remains considerably above the Fed’s 2% target. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index rose 3.6% on an annualized basis in September, while core PCE inflation, which excludes food and energy, stood at 3.1%.

Productivity Gains Could Eventually Ease Inflation, Says Jefferson

Despite the near-term price pressures, Jefferson expects AI adoption to eventually expand the economy's productive capacity and help moderate inflation.

As semiconductor manufacturers and other suppliers increase capacity to meet demand, supply constraints should ease. At the same time, wider AI adoption could help businesses produce more with fewer resources, lowering production costs.

“My baseline view is that adoption of new technology will ultimately lift the economy's productive capacity substantially but gradually,” Jefferson said, while cautioning that the timing and magnitude of those gains remain uncertain.

He also highlighted the potential consequences for monetary policy, arguing that if AI-driven productivity growth encourages businesses to invest more and households to spend more, it could push the economy's neutral interest rate higher.

For now, inflation remains his primary concern. Following the Fed's decision to hold interest rates steady at its October meeting, Jefferson said the latest economic data showed persistent price pressures.

“Accordingly, I see the trajectory of inflation as providing the more important signal for determining the appropriate stance of monetary policy,” he said.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, declined 0.63%; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) fell 0.83%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) was down 0.37%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘extremely bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

The Global X Artificial Intelligence & Technology ETF (AIQ) fell 1.29% on Friday, while the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (IYW) declined 1.32%.

data.title: Ramayana effect? Prime Focus Q2 results: Revenue rises to Rs.1,410.17 crore; PAT climbs to Rs.91.04 crore from Rs.5.8 crore
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- Prime Focus Ltd reported a consolidated net profit of Rs.58.27 crore in Q2 FY27. That was more than 14 times the Rs.4.06 crore it earned a year earlier. Strong demand for visual effects helped drive the increase in revenue and profit. Prime Focus is the parent company of visual effects and animation studio DNEG, the visual mastermind behind Ranbir Kapoor's Ramayana.

Consolidated revenue from operations rose 35.2% to Rs.1,410.17 crore in the September quarter. The company posted operating revenue of Rs.1,042.89 crore in the same quarter last year. Operating revenue rose by Rs.367.28 crore from the same quarter last year. Total income, including other income, increased from Rs.1,071.85 crore to Rs.1,446.59 crore.

Profit before tax (PAT) climbed to Rs.91.04 crore from Rs.5.8 crore a year earlier. The company also recorded an exceptional loss of Rs.2.11 crore during the September quarter. The latest results marked a turnaround from the preceding June quarter. Prime Focus had posted a consolidated net loss of Rs.45.78 crore in that quarter.

For the first half of FY27, consolidated operating revenue reached Rs.2,666.25 crore. That compares with Rs.2,019.71 crore in the same period a year earlier.

That was a Rs.646.54 crore year-on-year rise. First-half net profit fell from Rs.114.52 crore to Rs.12.49 crore, partly due to exceptional expenses. The June-quarter loss absorbed most of the September-quarter profit.

Prime Focus disclosed raids by the Income Tax Department from October 7 to 14. The raids covered certain company offices and the homes of some directors. The department also seized some electronic records during the operation.

The company said it had cooperated with tax officials and supplied the documents they needed. Prime Focus said it had received no order when it approved the results.

It also said that it had received no demand or show-cause notice related to the search. The company saw no need to adjust its financial results following the proceedings.

Prime Focus Studios is producing the two-part Ramayana adaptation with Yash's Monster Mind Creations. DNEG is among the visual effects partners on the project. The studio lists Ramayana among its released projects, alongside Sky Force and Fighter.

Other released projects include Motor City, Eden and William Tell. The list also includes Those About to Die and The Garfield Movie. It also features Brahmāstra: Part One - Shiva.

The studio lists eight projects in production. These include The Angry Birds Movie 3, CoComelon: The Movie and The Garfield Movie 2. Animal Friends and Black Palace are also in production. The remaining titles are Blood on Snow, Bollywoof and Above the Below.

data.title: Bitcoin ETFs shed $2.35B in two weeks as BlackRock’s losing streak hits 11 sessions
data.description:
US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded $2.35 billion in net outflows over two consecutive weeks, as redemptions reached more than $1 billion each week.

According to Farside Investors data, spot Bitcoin ETFs shed $1.07 billion between Nov. 9 and Nov. 13, following $1.28 billion in outflows the previous week, the largest weekly redemptions since late June.

The funds recorded $185.4 million in net outflows on Friday, down from $284.1 million on Thursday and $299.8 million on Wednesday. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $143.5 million of Friday’s withdrawals, while Fidelity’s Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC) shed $41.9 million.

Friday marked the seventh consecutive trading session of net withdrawals, with about $1.71 billion redeemed since Nov. 5. The sustained outflows coincided with broader market weakness as Bitcoin fell below $70,000 on the same day.

BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF extends losing streak to 11 sessions

IBIT’s $143.5 million in net outflows on Friday extended the fund’s withdrawal streak to 11 consecutive trading sessions since Oct. 30.

The latest losses brought IBIT’s total net outflows over the 11-session streak to about $2.35 billion, extending withdrawals after outflows crossed the $2 billion mark on Wednesday.

IBIT shed $908.4 million during the latest week, following approximately $1.21 billion in withdrawals the previous week. Its November outflows reached $2.12 billion, accounting for roughly 90% of the broader Bitcoin ETF market’s net withdrawals during the month.

data.title: Strive CEO Says Bitcoin Could ‘Go To A Penny’ And The Company Would Still Survive Because It Has No Debt
data.description:
Key points:
  • Matt Cole said on Thursday that because Strive has preferred equity only, they have “no liquidation point.”
  • Strive has two securities, including SATA and SATS, which pays 13% and 15% dividends, respectively.
  • Cole said Strive had planned for Bitcoin falling as much as 80%.

Strive Inc. (ASST) CEO Matt Cole said that Bitcoin (BTC) “could literally go to a penny,” and the treasury company would still survive because it carries no debt that could force it to sell.

Speaking with Anthony Pompliano on the Pomp Podcast on Thursday, Cole explained that Strive raises money only through preferred stock, so there is no price at which its Bitcoin would be seized. “Because we have preferred equity only, no debt. We have no liquidation point,” he said.

He compared that to borrowing against Bitcoin, where a sharp drop can wipe out traders. “We see this in the coin markets every time it’s dropped. How many billions of dollars gets liquidated?” Cole said.

Strive has two such securities, Variable Rate Series A Perpetual Preferred Stock (SATA), which pays a variable 13% that rises to 13.25% in December, and Series A Perpetual SATS Preferred Stock (SATS), which pays 15%.

ASST stock was trading over 1% down in overnight trading, after closing down 4% on Friday. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around ASST remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘low’ levels over the past day.

Built To Ride Out Bear Markets

Cole said Strive planned for Bitcoin to fall as much as 80%. To do that, it keeps about 85% to 90% of its balance sheet in Bitcoin and 10% to 15% in cash, which can cover its obligations during a downturn. “We could ride out any historical bear market without even having to sell a single Bitcoin,” he said. He added that the approach might even be too cautious. “Even if we had to sell 2% or 5%, that’s probably a reasonable risk for a company. You’re not blowing up,” Cole said.

Cole has made a similar case before. In June, he said Strive could keep paying dividends through a bear market mimicking one like 2022-23 using cash reserves, without selling Bitcoin.

A Bet Against The Dollar

Cole described the company’s structure as a long-term wager against the U.S. currency. Strive sells perpetual preferred stock, which pays dividends with no end date. “They will never stop debasing the U.S. dollar, and so we are perpetually short the U.S. dollar because we are selling a perpetual preferred equity, which will pay dividend forever,” he said.

Cole said Bitcoin needs to rise faster than SATA’s and SATS’s dividend rates over time for the company’s common shareholders to benefit.

That cushion is already being tested. Strive held 43,153 BTC bought at an average cost of $87,821 per coin. With Bitcoin’s price trading near $67,018 at the time of writing, that’s about 24% below Strive’s average purchase price.

On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘extremely bearish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘high’ levels over the past day.

data.title: Swiggy, Zepto, Eternal rivals on same board: What govt's new gig worker welfare panel means
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- Swiggy, Zepto and Eternal may compete for customers in India's quick commerce and food delivery markets, but representatives of the three companies will now share a platform to discuss the welfare of gig and platform workers.

In a LinkedIn post, Madhav Kasturia, founder and CEO Zippee, highlighted the constitution of the National Social Security Board for Unorganised Workers and Gig and Platform Workers, saying the government has brought competing platforms together to deliberate on social security for delivery partners and other gig workers.

While the government notification has not provided any names for the members of the board, Kasturia mentioned that Swiggy, Zepto and Eternal are on it.

The 22-member board includes representatives from Swiggy, Zepto and Eternal, as well as Urban Company, Rapido and workers' organisations, Kasturia said.

The Ministry of Labour and Employment notified the constitution of the board on October 30 under the Code on Social Security. The statutory body will recommend and monitor welfare schemes for unorganised workers, gig workers and platform workers.

These schemes could cover health and maternity benefits, accident and disability insurance, life insurance and old-age protection, according to Kasturia's post.

The development also has financial implications for aggregator companies. Kasturia pointed to provisions under the Social Security Code that require aggregators to contribute 1-2% of their annual turnover, subject to a cap of 5% of payments made or payable to gig workers.

The applicable contribution rate and the date from which it will take effect are yet to be notified, he said.

Such contributions could add to the costs platforms need to account for in their delivery economics.

Kasturia also flagged a practical challenge -- gig workers may work with multiple platforms, move between cities or switch between full-time employment and gig work. Ensuring that their records, eligibility and insurance benefits remain accessible across these transitions will be important.

The government's notification assigns the board the task of recommending suitable welfare schemes, advising the Centre on matters related to the Code and monitoring social welfare schemes. It will also review record-keeping functions at the state level and expenditure from the relevant fund and account.

The board is required to meet at least three times a year.

Kasturia said the recommendations and their implementation would determine how easily delivery partners can access these benefits when they need them.

data.title: US spot Bitcoin ETFs bleed $185 million as outflow streak hits seven days
data.description:
US spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $185 million in net outflows on November 13. That made it seven straight trading days of investors heading for the exits.

Ethereum ETFs, meanwhile, pulled in $2.36 million on the same day. It is not exactly a stampede in the other direction, but in a week like this, any green on the board stands out.

The more precise figure from flow trackers, including Farside Investors, puts the Bitcoin ETF outflow at $185.4 million. Nearly all of it came from the two biggest names in the business.

BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) led the retreat with a $143.5 million withdrawal. Fidelity's Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC) came second with $41.9 million in outflows.

Add those two together and you get the full $185.4 million. Every other spot Bitcoin ETF reported zero net flows for the day.

Across the full seven-day losing streak, Bitcoin ETFs shed roughly $1.91 billion. November 13's $185.4 million was less than a tenth of that total, which says something about how heavy the earlier days in the run were.

Zoom out to the month and the number gets bigger. Cumulative outflows for November have exceeded $2 billion month-to-date.

All of this happened while Bitcoin itself traded in a range of $68,000 to $73,000.

On the Ethereum side, the inflow was reported at approximately $2.3 million to $2.36 million depending on the tracker.

Spot Bitcoin ETFs launched in the US in January 2024, and since then they have attracted net inflows of about $54.8 billion to $55 billion.

That cumulative figure has held up despite repeated outflow streaks throughout 2026. The current seven-day drain of roughly $1.91 billion represents a small slice of the total capital these products have gathered, under 4% of lifetime net inflows.

The research findings describe the outflows as pointing to growing wariness among institutional investors, driven by volatility and uncertainty around Bitcoin's price in recent weeks.

The concentration in IBIT and FBTC is the detail worth watching. When the two largest products account for 100% of a day's outflows, it suggests the selling is coming from a specific class of holder rather than a broad-based exodus across every fund.

The research notes the modest Ethereum inflows may hint at a shift in investor sentiment toward other crypto assets. A $2.36 million inflow against a $185.4 million outflow is not a rotation so much as a footnote, and one day of data does not make a trend.

data.title: Pfizer, Innovent GLP-1 drugs added to China national insurance for diabetes
data.description:
GLP-1 drugs from Pfizer and Innovent Biologics will be added to China's state-run health insurance scheme from January 1 for patients with type 2 diabetes, the National Healthcare Security Administration said on Saturday, in a fresh challenge to Danish rival Novo Nordisk .

China has the highest number of adults with diabetes in the world, ​according to an estimate by the International Diabetes Federation. Pfizer's ecnoglutide and Innovent's mazdutide belong to the class of GLP-1 ​receptor agonist drugs already included in China's state insurance list from firms such ​as Novo, Eli Lilly and Guangzhou Innogen Pharmaceutical .

Novo's Ozempic joined China's reimbursement list in ​2022, followed by Lilly's Mounjaro and Innogen's efsubaglutide alfa from this year for patients with ​type 2 diabetes. Inclusion in the national reimbursement list makes drugs more widely available ‌in ⁠the country of 1.4 billion people, though an increase in sales volume often comes with lower prices.

The GLP-1 class of weight drugs mimics a gut ⁠hormone to curb appetite and regulate blood sugar in patients with diabetes.

Sales of Ozempic injector pens in the greater China region of mainland China, Taiwan and Hong Kong — Novo's largest market after the US — slipped 7% to about 5.4 billion Danish crowns ($850 ​million) in 2025.

Other treatments to be added to the list include two Eli Lilly drugs for ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease, as well as a CAR-T therapy from JW Therapeutics , according to company statements.

The CAR-T therapy, which engineers patients' immune cells to recognise and kill cancer cells, was the first to be included in the reimbursement list.

data.title: Tesla Cybercab Now Available For Purchase For Select Customers — But There’s A Catch
data.description:
Key points:
  • Tesla announced that “select customers are now being invited to purchase Cybercab for personal use” at an estimated price of $29,990.
  • Buyers will also need to pay a $1,000 nonrefundable deposit and subscribe to Tesla's autonomous driving software for $299 per month.
  • The company estimates that deliveries will begin in December.

Tesla Inc. (TSLA) has begun inviting select customers to purchase its fully autonomous Cybercab, marking a new step in Elon Musk's long-promised robotaxi ambitions.

However, owning the futuristic, two-seater vehicle comes with some significant limitations, including a mandatory monthly software subscription and restrictions on where it can operate.

Tesla shares declined nearly 2% in Friday’s regular trading, while falling another 1% in the afterhours session.

Tesla Cybercab Comes With $299 Monthly Subscription

In posts on X on Friday, Tesla announced that “select customers are now being invited to purchase Cybercab for personal use” at an estimated price of $29,990.

Buyers will also need to pay a $1,000 nonrefundable deposit and subscribe to Tesla's autonomous driving software for $299 per month.

The company estimates that deliveries will begin in December.

The two-door vehicle, which has no steering wheel or pedals, was previously deployed exclusively in Tesla's robotaxi fleet.

However, personal ownership does not mean buyers can immediately use the vehicles anywhere they want. Tesla clarified in the fine print that personally owned Cybercabs will only operate “in supported service areas.”

Ashok Elluswamy, Tesla's head of AI, added that the vehicles will “work unsupervised inside all the same geo locations as” the company's existing Robotaxi service.

There is also a catch for prospective buyers hoping to turn their vehicles into money-making robotaxis. Tesla's current personal-use offering does not allow owners to immediately operate them as commercial fleet vehicles.

Regulatory Hurdles And Robotaxi Ambitions

The announcement comes after years of promises from Musk about bringing fully autonomous vehicles to consumers.

In 2016, Tesla claimed that all vehicles it was producing had the hardware necessary to become fully self-driving. Three years later, Musk predicted the company would have “over a million robotaxis” on the roads by 2020.

Those ambitions have yet to fully materialize, although Tesla has made progress with its Robotaxi service, which began operating Model Y SUVs in Austin, Texas, in June 2025 before expanding to other cities in Texas and Florida.

Wood Says Tesla Robotaxis Have Hit 'Escape Velocity'

Wood said ARK Invest has been using the recent correction in Tesla to increase its exposure to the company rather than retreat from its bets on Musk.

"If anything, Robotaxi has hit escape velocity delighting consumers. This is the moment we've been waiting for, so we're not worried there," Wood said. Her optimism comes despite Tesla stock tumbling more than 10% over the past week.

Wood acknowledged that Musk could face political distractions, including potentially being called to testify, but argued that his ability to manage multiple responsibilities sets him apart.

"He is a maestro at compartmentalization like no one else I've ever seen," she said.

What Retail Investors Think Of TSLA Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Tesla trended in the ‘bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

TSLA stock is down 12% year-to-date and 13% over the past 12 months. The S&P 500 ETF (SPY) and the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) are up 12% over the past 12 months.

data.title: How Apple became the safe ‘Costco’ of tech. Bernstein says keep buying
data.description:
Apple is starting to appeal to investors looking for a safe haven from higher-flying, higher-risk artificial intelligence stocks, according to a recent note by Bernstein.

The analysis comes as Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia rattles the AI trade, adding to recent investor anxiety surrounding tech stocks in general.

"With little correlation to tech peers, Apple now trades in line with high quality consumer stocks," Bernstein analysts led by Mark Newman said in a report on Thursday.

Apple had a strong run even after John Ternus succeeded Tim Cook as CEO, and it faced rising memory costs and narrower margins. Unlike other "Magnificent Seven" companies, the iPhone maker has earned safe haven status thanks to a lack of correlation with tech peers that are spending hundreds of billions of dollars in capital expenditures.

At Apple, capex is less than 2% of revenue.

As a result, shares in the largest company in the U.S. by market value have benefited from the recent AI sell-off, sending its price-to-earnings multiple to all-time highs.

Bernstein reiterated an outperform rating on Apple in the report, and a $380 price target, implying about 7% upside from Thursday's close.

Costco of tech

"The market has long decoupled Apple from the rest of the mega-cap tech names and reclassified Apple to a consumer compounder," Newman said.

Apple currently trades in line with consumer stocks on revenue growth, while its earnings and free cash flow, or FCF, growth sit modestly above the line. Apple's current valuation is 37 times its expected earnings per share for 2027 and roughly twice the market's forward earnings multiple.

Among companies with a market capitalisation above $200 billion and consensus future EPS growth of below 15%, four companies exceed a forward P/E of 30, namely Costco at 46 times, Walmart at 39 times, Apple at 37 times and General Electric at 36 times, according to Bernstein.

Apple's expected annual revenue growth through 2029 is roughly 9%, faster than Costco's 7% and Walmart's 5%.

Apple also wins on free cash flow generation and shareholder returns. With an estimated 3.1% FCF yield and stock buybacks equal to 3% of total market capitalisation in 2027 and 3.2% in 2028, Apple is expected to return almost all of its free cash flow to shareholders through buybacks and dividends.

Newman said Apple exhibits many characteristics of a consumer staples stock, such as predictable replacement demand, pricing power with suppliers and customers, relatively low investment needs and steady cash returns to shareholders. Together, these traits make its earnings more dependable, he said.

Bernstein's smartphone survey found that 90% of iPhone users stayed with the brand when replacing their previous device. Similarly, Costco's worldwide annual membership renewal rate is also about 90%, and the market puts a 40 times earnings multiple on Costco, Bernstein said.

"On forward revenue growth metric, Apple is now the fastest growing company if put in the consumer universe and trades in-line with the rest of its peers on a revenue growth adjusted basis; on earnings and FCF growth it sits modestly above the line, alongside Ferrari and the scale retailers," Newman said.

data.title: JAPAN MATERIAL: Q2 sales rose 20.4%, while operating profit grew 41.0% on semiconductor-fab demand

data.title: Markets Espresso: Yaar ne hi loot lia ghar yaar ka ft. Nvidia shareholders
data.description:
Hello there, Espresso Lovers! The Diwali festivities are done; we are back to the grind, and it almost feels as if, for all the chilling we did during those 5-7 days, the news flow since Tuesday has made up for all of that, just to ensure that we do not get carried away with all the laziness!

It feels good when your optimism pays off, doesn't it? Around the same time last month, our Espresso spoke about the underperforming largecaps and how investors have only faced disappointment since the Nifty topped in September 2024, and how the only way forward will be higher. Since then, the Nifty is up over 3,000 points, the Nifty Bank is at the cusp of a record high, ICICI Bank is already at record highs, and most other largecaps are up between 10% and 20% over the last few sessions. To all those who stuck around, your patience has just started to pay off. Of course, it's not celebratory yet, but for stocks that have not delivered anything in years, you'd take 10-15% in days with both hands!

But this week has only been about one man and his antics. Jensen Huang's fall from grace has been faster and swifter than anyone that comes to mind, not even Lance Armstrong! The face of the AI revolution has now become the face of scandal, speculation, gossip and endless scrutiny of how things eventually ran at Nvidia, which, from a nondescript start-up supplying gaming chips, became the most valuable company in the world in a matter of years. As Arshad Warsi mocked Ajay Devgan in Golmaal Returns (2008): "Man of the house se, man out of the house. Pent house se tent house!" Talk about falling off a cliff? Yup, exactly that.

For a man who did subah ka nashta in one country, jetted off to have dopehar ka khana in another, and had raat ka dinner in a third country, now finds himself out of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. From private jets, Huang will now have to spend the near future addressing congressional hearings, court subpoenas, and multiple investigations involving national security, considering one of his many (yes, it wasn't only one) affairs was with a woman whom US intelligence claims is a Chinese spy.

The real winner in this? Of course, Nvidia's competitors - AMD, Broadcom and Alphabet- but no, that's not the answer. India's meme factory is the actual winner, and they have had a ball tripping on this entire scandal with one hilarious video after another that are spread across social media.

Yes, there has been a loss of face, loss of reputation, and many other losses, but the real loser in all of this, as has always been the case, is the small shareholder. Nvidia has lost nearly $1.5 trillion in market capitalisation since the scandal came to light, and closed below $4 trillion in value for the first time after June last year. They trusted the man, not the company, and the man has betrayed their trust, as in his own words. There have been such instances in the past of other companies facing similar challenges and them having overcome the same as well. But for Nvidia, this will be tough, very, very tough.

Okay, enough with Nvidia. Back to our markets. The recent rebound seen in the largecap names has taken everyone by surprise. The bigger surprise, though, has been the newfound love for India among Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs). In just 10 sessions, FPIs have poured in $9 billion. $9 billion?! Not as if anything changed in the last 10 sessions, and neither is India the only market they could invest in! Is this a record? Almost there. The most FPIs have bought in a single month in India is $9.6 billion, which, incidentally, also happened in November 2020. But what is with this newfound love? We try to decode that in our latest Editor's Playbook.

While everybody was still reeling from the Jensen Huang aftermath, Microsoft suddenly decided to get into Friday mode/airplane mode / go MIA, whatever. Everything went down - from mail to Teams, and everything Microsoft. The worst affected during this were the IT dudes. Every time something happened, their standard customer care response would be: MAIL DAALO. But who do we mail when the mails aren't working either? Every two hours, Microsoft would tweet saying work is in progress. The progress lasted a full 24 hours. Full services were only restored late night / early morning on Saturday. Did we function without a mailbox? Of course we did. For those who do a Teams call for the most random things every half hour, it was a dark day for them.

Today's is Children's Day. Our newsroom yesterday was the brightest, the happiest, and the cutest it has ever been during the 365 days of the year! The wonderful children of our colleagues were in the studios yesterday, sharing their hopes, ambitions, and dreams, and they are definitely worth taking note. Two girls want to be cricketers, one wants to be a marine biologist, another a space scientist, another a gymnast, but then they are children after all; they only demand what we demanded when we were kids - A little more TV time, some more play time, and of course, feed us desserts and some Maggi! You can catch all of those heartwarming clips on our social media handles! To all the kids out there, you are the future; the world is yours to conquer! A Happy Happy Children's Day to every child out there!

That's all for this week! Earnings season is over, but newsflow will ensure we are never starved of content. There's a lot happening on the global front, and who knows what further twists lie in the Jensen Huang saga. Maybe Abbas-Mastan are watching this very closely! But we'll be back as always on Saturday with the latest brew! Until then, so long and take good care of yourselves, and feed a piece of cake to your children!

data.title: Zai Lab Announces First-Time Inclusion of KarXT and VYVGART Hytrulo® in China's 2026 National Reimbursement Drug List, Expanding Access to Key Growth Products
data.description:
SHANGHAI and CAMBRIDGE, Mass, Nov. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Zai Lab Limited (; ), an innovation-driven, global biopharma company, today announced that five of its commercial medicines in China have been included in the country's 2026 National Reimbursement Drug List (NRDL). The update includes two first-time listings, expanding patient access to treatments for gMG and schizophrenia, and three renewals, which maintain access across oncology and infectious disease.

Zai Lab Products Newly Added or Renewed in 2026 NRDL:

First-time listings:

  • VYVGART Hytrulo® (efgartigimod alfa, subcutaneous injection): for the treatment of adult patients with anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody-positive generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG).
  • KarXT (xanomeline and trospium chloride capsules): for the treatment of schizophrenia in adults.

Renewals:

  • NUZYRA® (omadacycline for injection): for the treatment of community-acquired bacterial pneumonia and acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections.
  • QINLOCK® (ripretinib tablets): for the treatment of adult patients with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) who have received prior treatment with three or more kinase inhibitors, including imatinib.
  • AUGTYRO® (repotrectinib capsules): for the treatment of adult patients with ROS1-positive locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and adult patients with solid tumors harboring a neurotrophic tyrosine receptor kinase (NTRK) gene fusion.

"The inclusion of KarXT and VYVGART Hytrulo in the NRDL represents an important milestone for Zai Lab and the patients we serve," said Dr. Yizhe Wang, Zai Lab Operating Partner. "These listings will help broaden access to two important therapies, including KarXT's novel mechanism of action for schizophrenia and the convenience of VYVGART Hytrulo's subcutaneous administration for patients with gMG. Together with the renewal of our other listed products, we are grateful to the National Healthcare Security Administration for its continued support of innovative medicines and remain committed to delivering greater benefit to patients."

The 2026 National Reimbursement Drug List will take effect on January 1, 2027.

  • Notice:

  • *xanomeline and trospium chloride capsules included in the 2026 NRDL covers the following specifications: (I) xanomeline tartrate 50 mg (calculated as C14H23N3OS) and trospium chloride 20 mg per capsule; (II) xanomeline tartrate 100 mg (as C14H23N3OS) and trospium chloride 20 mg per capsule; (III) xanomeline tartrate 125 mg (as C14H23N3OS) and trospium chloride 30 mg per capsule. All are indicated for schizophrenia in adults.

  • *For AUGTYRO® included in the 2026 NRDL, the reimbursement scope for adult patients with NTRK gene fusion-positive solid tumors is specifically: adult patients diagnosed, by a well-validated testing method, with solid tumors harboring a neurotrophic tyrosine receptor kinase (NTRK) gene fusion, and who meet one of the following conditions: having locally advanced or metastatic disease, or for whom surgical resection is likely to result in severe complications, or who have failed prior treatment or have no satisfactory alternative treatment options.

About Zai Lab

Zai Lab Limited (; ) is an innovative, research-based, commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company based in China and the United States. We are focused on discovering, developing, and commercializing innovative products that address medical conditions with significant unmet needs in the areas of oncology, immunology, neuroscience, and infectious disease. Our goal is to leverage our competencies and resources to positively impact human health.

For additional information about Zai Lab, please visit www.zailaboratory.com or follow us at www.linkedin.com/company/zai-lab or https://x.com/ZaiLab_Global.

data.title: Softbank further trims India exposure, offloads Meesho shares worth ₹1,885 cr
data.description:
Japanese investor SoftBank Group has sold 1.65 per cent stake in Meesho for ₹1,885 crore, further trimming its investments in India's e-commerce sector.

In the latest transaction, SVF II Meerkat (DE) LLC, an affiliate of SoftBank, offloaded 7.64 crore shares in Bengaluru-based Meesho, according to the block deal data on the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The share sale was executed on Friday at an average price of ₹246.75 apiece, taking the total deal value to ₹1,885.17 crore.

With this, the affiliate's holding in Meesho has fallen to 5.19 per cent from 6.84 per cent.

The stake sale, however, found buyers, with a clutch of domestic and foreign institutional investors participating in the transaction, with Societe Generale (SocGen) emerging as the largest buyer.

Paris-based financial services firm SocGen picked up more than 1.47 crore shares, or a 0.32 per cent stake, for ₹364.65 crore.

Domestic institutional buyers included mutual funds managed by Motilal Oswal, HDFC, Edelweiss and Aditya Birla Sun Life, along with Bajaj Life Insurance.

Overseas participants included Morgan Stanley, Fidelity Investments, BNP Paribas, Goldman Sachs, Ghisallo Capital Management, William Blair Investment Management and Texas Municipal Retirement System.

The Singaporean government, Monetary Authority of Singapore and Norway's sovereign wealth fund Government Pension Fund Global, also participated in the transaction.

Meesho shares rose 1.53 per cent to close at ₹257.99 apiece on the NSE on Friday.

The latest transaction adds to a series of stake sales by SoftBank in its Indian portfolio companies, particularly in the e-commerce and consumer technology space.

Earlier this month, the Japanese investor pared a 1.56 per cent stake in eyewear retailer Lenskart Solutions for ₹1,896 crore. Before that, in September, it sold a 1.7 per cent stake in Meesho for ₹1,650 crore.

SoftBank had also divested nearly a 2.6 per cent stake in Lenskart for ₹2,888 crore in August and a further 3.25 per cent stake for ₹2,873 crore in June.

In January, the technology investor reduced its shareholding in electric two-wheeler maker Ola Electric Mobility by 2.15 per cent, continuing its broader portfolio monetisation exercise in the country.

data.title: India's current account deficit seen widening to USD 57 billion in FY27 on higher imports: ICICI Bank
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- India's current account deficit (CAD) is expected to widen to USD 57 billion, or 1.4 per cent of GDP, in FY27 as stronger domestic demand and higher oil prices keep imports elevated despite robust export growth, according to a report by ICICI Bank.

The bank also expects India's goods trade deficit to reach USD 380 billion during the financial year, compared with its earlier estimate of USD 388 billion, with gold imports likely to remain moderate.

"Goods exports have seen a stellar performance in the fiscal year so far (22% YoY), but stronger domestic demand and higher oil prices have driven goods imports higher too (16% YoY)," the report said.

India's merchandise trade deficit widened to nearly USD 40 billion in October, its highest level in 12 months, from USD 30.2 billion in September. The increase was driven by a higher oil deficit of USD 14 billion and a non-oil, non-gold deficit of USD 20 billion.

Goods exports rose 45 per cent year-on-year to a record USD 49 billion in October, supported by a 140 per cent jump in oil shipments and 33 per cent growth in non-oil exports.

However, goods imports increased 17 per cent to a record USD 89 billion, with oil imports rising 54 per cent and non-oil, non-gold imports growing 29 per cent.

The report said services exports are likely to record moderate growth amid softer demand due to disruptions from artificial intelligence, while remittances are expected to remain steady. Net services exports rose 13 per cent year-on-year to USD 19.8 billion in October.

On the external financing front, the bank said the recent turnaround in foreign portfolio investment (FPI) flows had improved the outlook for the rupee. India received FPI inflows of USD 8.8 billion in November so far, following a period of outflows.

"This makes us more constructive on INR, along with the recent measures by RBI," the report said, while cautioning that any escalation in the West Asia conflict could pose a near-term concern.

The bank noted that India's balance of payments remained in surplus during the first half of FY27, supported by strong banking capital inflows, including deposits under the FCNR scheme.

data.title: Microsoft says consumer products services recovered; still monitoring enterprise services
data.description:
Microsoft said its consumer products services had fully recovered at 4:10 p.m. UTC on Friday (1610 GMT), while it was seeing some sustained recovery for its Microsoft 365 enterprise services.

The technology giant said it was "monitoring the backlog of email messages accrued during this event" before considering the issue with the enterprise services resolved.

"Due to the severity of impact this incident caused, we're monitoring for an extended period to ensure no additional mitigative actions are required," Microsoft said in an update on its service status page.

data.title: BOE likely to raise rates further in 2027, Pill tells FT
data.description:
The Bank of England will probably need to raise interest rates further in 2027 on top of an increase in December to combat inflation, Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill told the Financial Times in an interview published on Saturday.

“My view would be we will see evidence that motivates further rises” Pill told the newspaper, referring to the need for rate hikes next year, given the risks of second-round effects from elevated energy costs.

“We will do what is necessary to get inflation back to 2% through time.”
